subject.title: PR4/5 durable core: wake controls, inspection, CLI, and Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw ship this opt-in durable runtime and its read-only operator inspection surface in core on the 2026.7.1 release line?
rationale: The change introduces a new core runtime mode, shared persistent schema, public Gateway protocol, CLI surface, and long-term recovery contract; tests cannot determine whether maintainers want to own that product and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Sponsor inspection-first stack
options.body: Approve the durable-core direction, retain the read-only PR4 boundary, and require dependency-order landing plus exact-head live upgrade and inspection proof.

options.title: Defer release inclusion
options.body: Keep the design work open but move implementation off the 2026.7.1 release line until the complete lifecycle and rollback plan is ready.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Close the stack if maintainers do not want OpenClaw core to own this additional durable runtime and persistence contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor inspection-first stack
recommendation.body: Approve the durable-core direction, retain the read-only PR4 boundary, and require dependency-order landing plus exact-head live upgrade and inspection proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-wide product, release, Gateway protocol, and persistence decision rather than a narrow component repair.
